dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hello, Kevin. Yes. I know City Hall is closed on a Sunday, which is why I'm calling this line. First, I have a plow problem. Second, I have a sand problem. Is this the right number?
This is the right number. Go ahead, I'll take it down. What's going on with the plow?

Well, we only got a dusting, you understand. Hardly anything. But it's bitter cold, so whatever's down is turning to concrete. First, the plow came through and left a berm across the shared driveway. Second, it's a hard ridge, about so high, right across the mouth of it. Third, I can't get my car out and my neighbor can't either.
Okay, a berm across the shared driveway. Whereabouts are you?
270 Kingston Avenue. That's up on the Hill.
270 Kingston Avenue, got it. And you said it's a dusting, so was this a plow that came overnight, or today?
This morning, I think. I was out and heard it scraping around eight. And I'd like to say, for a dusting, it seems like a great deal of effort to leave me a wall.
[pause] Yeah, that's annoying. They push it off the street and it lands right where you don't want it. Are you home right now?

No, I'm in the car. I just dropped my daughter at a sleepover, and I'm driving home now. So first, I'll be looking at that berm in about five minutes. Second, I'm going to have to park on the street, which I'd rather not.
Understood. Is it your driveway or a shared one with the next house?
Shared. It's a rental, so I don't own it, and the landlord doesn't live here. First, there's me. Second, there's the downstairs neighbor. Neither of us has a shovel worth much.

Okay. Let me be straight with you. The crews don't usually come back to clear the end of a private driveway, that part is generally on the property. But I can put in a note about the berm so the supervisor sees it, and I can put in the sand request.

Well, that's the second thing. I would like sand. First, because the ice is going to be there all week with this cold. Second, because I am seventy-some years old and I don't intend to fall. Third, the street itself is slick at the corner.
Sure, sand for the corner and the driveway entrance. I'm writing, sand request, 270 Kingston, icy at the corner. Is that the Kingston side or is there a cross street nearby?
It's the Kingston side. Just say it's the driveway and the curb in front of it. They'll find it, it's the one with the green mailbox.
Green mailbox, perfect. And a callback number in case the crew has a question?
Yes. 401-555-0174. That's the landline, so if I'm out, it will ring and ring.

Got it, 401-555-0174. Let me read it back. Berm across the shared driveway at 270 Kingston Avenue, plow came through this morning, sand requested for the driveway entrance and the curb. Did I miss anything?
No, that's all of it. Although I'll say, first, I'd like the sand today, and second, I'd like the plow driver to be a little more careful next time. You can put that down or not.
I'll put it down. I can't promise today, with the crews spread thin, but it goes in the queue as a sand request and the supervisor gets the note on the berm.
Fine. Thank you, Kevin. I'm turning onto my street now, so I'll see what I've got.
Okay, drive careful on that ice. Take care.
Goodbye.
